stories.title: Baron's disallowed buzzer shot in Orlando
beats: Game 3 of the 2002 first round in Orlando is tied with 0.7 seconds left and a sideline inbound.
Baron says he was not even supposed to get the ball; with T-Mac guarding him he pushed off, doubled back to the top and caught it.
He shot, watched it bank in, and says the red light did not come on until the ball nearly hit the backboard.
He popped his collar, then saw the referee waving it off, and ran at the referee cussing.
He names the referee as Bernie Fryer; a postgame line is read: 'You can rely on the clock, but I'm going to rely on my judgment.'

stories.title: Ejected for clapping, then Stephen Jackson walks in
beats: Baron recalls a small, mean referee who threw him out of a playoff game for clapping; the hosts identify him from a photo as Joey Crawford.
The ref said 'Stop clapping,' then 'Oop, you're gone.' Baron places it in the Dallas series.

stories.title: Meeting Tim Duncan at Ohio State camp
beats: In 1992, during the Rodney King riots, Baron, a South Central kid at Crossroads, had school cancelled in Santa Monica.
His history teacher mailed him a plane ticket to an Ohio State basketball camp for the second week of the riots, and he went alone.
At camp a quiet ninth- or tenth-grader named Tim Duncan won every award, including MVP, while everyone talked about other recruits.
Baron told him he had game; the only thing he remembers Duncan saying was 'Thank you, man' (and, years later in a game while Baron was going at Bruce Bowen, 'shut up').
He says Jim Jackson was a camp counselor who showed up when he wanted, with another player the caption calls 'Thunderberg'.

stories.title: The Weather Channel in the Knicks locker room
beats: Jeremy Lin's locker was next to Baron's, with one empty locker between them, so Baron watched Linsanity up close.
Once Lin's run started, Baron says about a thousand people crowded the locker room.
He lists CNN, MSNBC, MTV, BET, The Weather Channel, VH1 and a large Chinese press contingent.
He kept having to move his seat, ended up hanging his things in the handicap stall, and wondered what the Weather Channel was doing there.
The team eventually moved Lin into a full press-conference room.
stories.quote: damn what's the weather channel doing in here
stories.places: Knicks locker room, press conference room

stories.title: Baron tells Mike Montgomery to stop talking to him
beats: Under coach Mike Montgomery the Warriors held a team meeting where players stayed silent and Montgomery did all the talking.
Montgomery said 'everybody is saying this about you,' and Baron asked the room who actually had a problem with whom.
Baron got players to speak up, and he says the issues they had been taking to the coach were petty.
He then told Montgomery not to talk to him for the rest of the year and to send any message through the others.
He says he had 'disconnected this line'.
stories.quote: tell Mike Montgomery don't talk to me for the rest of the Year bro
stories.era: 2005-06 season (implied: the year before Don Nelson)

stories.title: The We Believe turnaround: partying on the court
beats: Chris Mullin promised to fix the team, and near the deadline the Warriors traded Troy Murphy, Mike Dunleavy and others for Stephen Jackson and Al Harrington.
They still lost; Don Nelson said he'd wait until next year, and Baron got hurt before All-Star weekend.
After a loss to Washington on two Gilbert Arenas free throws, the team met and Baron told them he'd throw a party at his birthday, but first they had to party on the court.
With Jackson, Harrington and Matt Barnes, players who never hung out started going out together and swapping NBA stories.
They beat Detroit, one of the league's best, and decided they could beat anybody.
stories.quote: if we make the the court our party and our club
stories.places: Washington (opponent), Detroit (opponent), clubs in every road city

stories.title: Mashburn's vertigo in Game 1
beats: Jamal Mashburn missed most of the season with an abdominal injury and came back for the playoffs.
In Game 1, within the first four minutes, he got vertigo and left the floor.
Baron, running down the court, yelled at him to come back: he's 'our guy', and the double teams he draws get Baron his points.
Mashburn was gone; Baron says they barely had a medical staff and nobody was coming into the locker room.
Baron says he was out for about a year after.
stories.quote: Hey, hey, hey, where you going?

stories.title: Baron's UCLA recruiting trip brawl
beats: On his UCLA recruiting visit, Baron's group played flag football against the softball team, and lost.
They went to the baseball players' place, 'like a frat house', and a big fight broke out.
Baron says it was eight or nine of them against 40 to 50 baseball players; he remembers standing on a little ledge as people came at him.
He says they were trying to make peace, he was confused, but 'right in the mix'.
He adds he also got into a fight the day before school started, in front of the dorms.
stories.quote: we just boxing with like 40 big old baseball dudes
stories.places: UCLA, baseball players' frat-like house, UCLA dorms

stories.title: Giving Jay-Z the black UCLA jersey
beats: A friend, Ivory, came over and brought Hip-Hop; one of them (caption unclear) asked if Baron wanted to meet Jay-Z, who wanted to wear his jersey. Baron says this was before people really wore jerseys.
They piled as many as fit into the car and went to a place the caption calls 'Cafe Mazz' to hang out with Jay.
Baron gave Jay his black UCLA jersey, which he says the older UCLA crowd hated, and a white one; they watched Jay pull off in his Range.
At the concert Jay came out in the jersey and everybody went crazy.
Backstage Baron met Method Man and Redman, and Redman gave him Hennessy.
stories.quote: at the concert he popped up with the jersey everybody was going crazy
stories.props: black UCLA jersey, white jersey, Range (Rover), Hennessy, the car
stories.era: UCLA years, 1997-99 (implied); a host says 'that summer'

stories.title: Elden Campbell orders barbecue at training camp
beats: Baron recalls the big men ordering barbecue during Hornets training camp.
After two days of practice Elden Campbell said they needed real food; the team didn't want to pay for it.
Campbell ordered barbecue after the second practice anyway.
The coach was furious: they were working to get in shape and the players were eating barbecue and sweet tea.
stories.quote: that dude ordered some barbecue after the second practice
stories.places: Hornets training camp (a host says Fort Mill)

stories.title: Jay-Z wears Baron's jersey (short version)
beats: At UCLA, a young A&R and big basketball fan known as Hip Hop told Baron that Jay-Z wanted to wear his jersey.
They drove down Sunset; Baron says Jay was young, cool, and on the Hard Knock Life tour.
Baron gave him the white jersey and the black UCLA jersey, and they were invited to the concert.
Backstage with a young Ja Rule and DMX, Baron was waiting for his moment, hoping Jay would bring him out on stage.
Jay came out in the jersey and everybody went nuts; Baron says it helped him win the LA crowd.
stories.quote: But when he showed up with the jersey, that was just everybody went nuts.
stories.props: white jersey, black UCLA jersey, 'the whip' (car)

stories.title: First dunk at five foot six
beats: In 10th grade, at about 5'6", he kept trying to dunk and missing, then finally dunked with a friend watching.
The friend told him to do it again, and he did.
He skipped class at Crossroads, a small school, and waited for his friends to get out for lunch.
In a lunchtime two-on-two he got his steps on the baseline and dunked on every big player on his team, who didn't know he could dunk.
Their faces looked 'like they lost their dog', and he decided to keep doing it.
stories.quote: So I dunked on every big dude on my team.

stories.title: First day at Golden State: 'like a damn funeral'
beats: When Baron arrived in Golden State he walked in around 10:15 for practice and nobody was on the court.
Players were still in the training room, one was lifting, some were on the bosu ball.
He told Chris Mullin it was like a damn funeral every day.
He told the team they'd run one play and otherwise just hoop and not look at the sideline.
He says he was back-to-back Player of the Week and they finished about 9-2, but out of the playoffs.
stories.quote: it's like a damn funeral like every day

stories.title: Ordering a well-done steak in a suit
beats: After his big contract in 2002, Baron says he started trying fine dining: wraps, falafel, seafood, wine.
He went to restaurants in suits with his feet hurting, doing things he wasn't comfortable with.
He sent back a pink steak and asked for it brown; he was asked, 'Are you sure?'
Everyone at the table acted like something was wrong with him: a man in a suit ordering a brown steak.
The bit ends with escargot and asking for ketchup, ranch or black pepper: 'The high life is not for me.'
stories.quote: Everybody at the table like, "Oh my god, something wrong with him.
stories.props: suit, steak, escargot, ketchup / ranch / black pepper

stories.title: Dunleavy yelling 'pass it' on the break
beats: Under Clippers coach Mike Dunleavy, who called every play, Baron pushed the ball on a fast break.
About to cross half court, all he heard from the bench was 'pass it, pass it'.
He saw nobody open, kept hearing it, then saw someone running and dropped the ball off by the hash.
The teammate was slow: Baron says it took him about seven (word unclear) to get to the rim.
Baron looked at the coach: leave me alone.
stories.quote: all you hear is going pass it pass it

stories.title: Welcome to the NBA: John Stockton
beats: Asked for his welcome-to-the-NBA moment, Baron names John Stockton.
He describes going for an inbound pass and thinking he had a steal; Stockton stole the ball from him (sequence partly garbled).
He says he could have played eight minutes that night, but the first two were turnover after turnover.
He went back in and it was the same: 'it was embarrassing'.
stories.quote: the first two minutes it was just turnover turnover turnover bucket

stories.title: Stockton humbles the rookie
beats: Baron says John Stockton made him question whether he knew how to play.
Stockton ripped him twice; a garbled passage follows about Baron going the wrong way for an outlet and a loose ball.
He was taken out of the game faster than ever before.
In person Stockton was much bigger than he looked on TV, like Steph Curry.
Stockton walked him to the same spot on the wing every time, pressured or not; Baron ends: 'i was glad when he was gone'.
stories.quote: john stockton embarrassed me dog

stories.title: Marbury: 'you can't guard me'
beats: As a rookie off the bench, Baron gave up an and-one to Stephon Marbury.
Marbury looked at him and said he didn't want any of this and couldn't guard him.
On the bench, Elden Campbell asked if he was going to let Marbury talk to him like that.
Baron got hot and was ready to fight.
stories.quote: he was like yeah you don't want none of this you can't guard me
stories.places: game vs Marbury's team (not named), Hornets bench

stories.title: 'Coach, you gotta play Jeremy Lin'
beats: With his back still messed up, Baron asked Mike D'Antoni for another week before activation; he says Lin was supposed to be cut when Baron was activated.
After a loss to Houston, Baron told D'Antoni to play Jeremy Lin; D'Antoni asked if he was out of his mind.
Baron argued Lin was the only guard who went 'north and south', unlike Toney Douglas and Iman Shumpert.
Lin played in the Houston game, had a small line in a 30-point loss, and Baron said that was enough to build on.
stories.quote: coach you gotta play Jeremy Lynn he was like you out your mind

stories.title: Hornets leaving Charlotte, flyers on Bourbon Street
beats: In 2002, with the Hornets about to move to New Orleans, Baron says home crowds fell to about 7,000-8,000 after 22,000 the year before.
In the next playoff series, against New Jersey, there were 5,000-6,000 people in the arena.
A host remembers anti-George Shinn t-shirts in the parking lot.
In New Orleans, Baron says people didn't know they had a team; players stood on Bourbon Street handing out flyers saying the Hornets were here.
He says they had to go make new fans.
stories.quote: Hey man, the Hornets are here.
stories.places: Charlotte arena, New Orleans, Bourbon Street

stories.title: Trading compliments with Bill Walton
beats: Baron says whenever he saw Bill Walton, he would do 'Bill Walton on Bill Walton'.
Walton would greet him with a stream of praise: one of the greatest guards in UCLA history, LA legend, explosive, smart, articulate.
Baron answered with Walton's own titles: NBA great, pioneer, UCLA aficionado, national champion, MVP.
Walton gave it right back; Baron says you couldn't beat him because he had the words.
stories.quote: I would do Bill Walton on Bill Walton

stories.title: Where 'We Believe' came from (Baron's version)
beats: Asked about the slogan, Baron says during their late playoff push a man held a 'We Believe' sign outside the arena as they arrived.
The phrase started picking up.
The players wanted We Believe shirts for Game 6 against Dallas.
He says the team was together off the court, at movies, out, at dinner, like it was their last season.
stories.quote: it was a dude like holding the sign out

stories.title: Calling the long-distance buzzer shot
beats: Broadcast audio: Baron's shot counts and is called as the longest shot in the NBA ('from 92 feet away' per the caption).
Watching it, Baron says he called it: he told a teammate he was going to make it and to just throw him the ball.
He points out Eddie Robinson with his hands up: the teammate he told to pass to him.
stories.quote: i called it tell my teammate i was gonna make it
stories.era: 2001 (from working title; not stated in transcript)

stories.title: Stephen Jackson and Al Harrington wake the team up (retelling)
beats: When Don Nelson was hired he called Baron: get in shape, he'd use him in the post and all over the floor; Baron thought of Run TMC.
The team was decent but couldn't beat anybody; Baron says the missing piece was the culture he'd had in New Orleans.
Stephen Jackson and Al Harrington arrived and woke everybody up: parties, the mall, eating out; before that nobody on the team hung out.
They took on a 'new rap group' persona: the court is the club, and if we win we go out.
Through the We Believe run they went out after wins, and fans partied with them.
stories.quote: we gonna have parties we going out we gonna hang out
stories.places: Oracle (sold out), clubs on the road

stories.title: In the Clippers locker room the night of the Sterling tape
beats: When the Sterling recording came out in 2014, Baron says he was at the Clippers game.
Doc Rivers told him to go talk to the players, and he went into the locker room.
He told them whatever they decided, even not playing, he would stand beside them.
He says they didn't look shaken; the feeling was 'what are we supposed to do?'
A passage about riding back on a private plane with the owner's right-hand man is garbled.
stories.quote: if y'all don't want to play I stand beside you
stories.places: Clippers locker room, a private plane (unclear)
stories.props: jerseys (garbled reference to taking them off), private plane

stories.title: Kirilenko's wink before the dunk
beats: Baron says as a kid on the dunk courts he learned that if he left the ground before the big men he could get over them; he wanted 'the biggest dude on the team'.
Asked how many times he has rewatched the dunk over AK-47, he says people tweet it to him every day.
He says Kirilenko 'asked for it': the play before, when Baron laid the ball up, Kirilenko gave him the big man's wink.
Baron's reaction at the time: 'All right, dog. I'm going to let that slide.'
stories.quote: He asked for it, because he winked at me to play before.
stories.places: dunk courts (childhood), playoff game (arena not named)
